name: Zo'é
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Souza, Dionizio Augusto B. (2003) Representacoes fonologicas na lingua Zo'e, MA thesis, Universidade de Sao Paulo (phonology; not found online)

new_statements.quote: 2.4 ACENTO. O acento em Jo'é é previsível. Raízes verbais, nominais e partículas têm a última sílaba acentuada: /pirɛ́/ [pirɛ́] 'peixe', /aɛsɛ́k/ [aɛsɛ́k] 'eu vejo', /tɛnã́/ [tɛnã́] 'apenas.'
new_statements.translation: 2.4 STRESS. Stress in Jo'é is predictable. Verbal roots, nominal roots and particles have the last syllable stressed: /pirɛ́/ 'fish', /aɛsɛ́k/ 'I see', /tɛnã́/ 'only'.
new_statements.citation: Cabral, Ana Suelly Arruda Câmara. 1996. Notas sobre a fonologia segmental do Jo'é. Moara (Revista dos Cursos de Pós-Graduação em Letras, UFPA, Belém) n. 4: 23-46.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK: Opened, rendered PDF page 10 (journal pp. 40-41) and read the image directly: left column, printed p. 40, heading '2.4 ACENTO.' followed by 'O acento em Jo'é é previsível. Raízes verbais, nominais e partículas têm a última sílaba acentuada: /pirέ/ [pirέ] 'peixe', /aεsέk/ [aεsέk] 'eu vejo', /tεnã́/ [tεnã́] 'apenas.'' — verbatim as reported (scanned lines 538-543 match apart from scanned garbling of IPA). Surrounding context read: §2.3 vowels before it, §2.5 (C)V(C) syllable patterns after it; p. 30 (§2.1.4.1) also confirmed: prenasalized allophones of /m n ŋ/ occur word-initially 'quando se segue na mesma palavra fonológica sílaba acentuada com um núcleo silábico oral'. IDENTITY…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the final syllable (of roots/particles; the example /a-ɛsɛ́k/ 'I see' shows a person prefix does not attract stress and a closed final syllable is stressed). Independently confirmed by the MNTB missionary description (Castro, Carvalho & Luz 2020: 'As palavras são acentuadas sempre na última sílaba') and consistent with Cabral 1998's final accent marks and with Sousa 2013: 110 'o Zo'é... conserva o acento final'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in any source read.
new_statements.exceptions: None in Cabral 1996. Cabral 2000 (not seen; summarized by Sousa 2013: 27-28) reportedly extends the accent domain to the phonological word including inflectional affixes and clitics, e.g. /d+ɔ-hɛ̃b-i/ 'ele não saiu' — implying suffixes/enclitics such as negative -i fall inside the stress domain (i.e., stress on the word-final syllable rather than root-final); this refinement could not be verified first-hand.
new_statements.domain_note: Cabral 1996 states the rule over roots (verbal, nominal) and particles in citation forms; Cabral 2000 (second-hand via Sousa 2013) makes the phonological word (root + inflectional affixes + clitics) the scope of accent. Castro et al. 2020 state it over 'palavras'. Note Cabral also uses 'acento nasal/oral' for suprasegmental nasality phonemes — distinct from stress ('acento tônico').
new_statements.identity_note: Cabral 1996/1998 use the older spelling 'Jo'é' [dʒoʔɛ] for the same language and community (Cuminapanema river, Pará; 131 speakers in 1992) now written Zo'é (glottocode zoee1240, ISO pto; earlier called Poturu). Single community, no dialect division reported.

sources.citation: Cabral, Ana Suelly Arruda Câmara. 1996. Notas sobre a fonologia segmental do Jo'é. Moara (Revista dos Cursos de Pós-Graduação em Letras, UFPA, Belém) n. 4: 23-46.
sources.quote: 2.4 ACENTO. O acento em Jo'é é previsível. Raízes verbais, nominais e partículas têm a última sílaba acentuada: /pirɛ́/ [pirɛ́] 'peixe', /aɛsɛ́k/ [aɛsɛ́k] 'eu vejo', /tɛnã́/ [tɛnã́] 'apenas.'
sources.note: §2.4 ACENTO, p. 40: stress is predictable; verbal roots, nominal roots and particles have the last syllable stressed (/pirɛ́/ 'peixe', /aɛsɛ́k/ 'eu vejo', /tɛnã́/ 'apenas'). Also p. 30: prenasalized allophones occur word-initially when a stressed syllable with oral nucleus follows in the same phonological word.

sources.citation: Castro, Onésimo Martins de; Carvalho, Carlos Alberto Lacerda; Luz, Edward Gomes da. 2020. Descrição morfológica da língua Zo'é. Anápolis: Missão Novas Tribos do Brasil; published on Recanto das Letras, texto T6954065 (3rd version, May 2020; data 1987-1991). https://www.recantodasletras.com.br/linguistica/6954065 (live page Cloudflare-blocked; read via Wayback snapshot 2024-03-03).
sources.note: Apresentação: 'As palavras são acentuadas sempre na última sílaba e entonação das frases serão descritas posteriormente' — words are always stressed on the last syllable. Independent (missionary) first-hand statement agreeing with Cabral.

sources.citation: Sousa, Suseile Andrade. 2013. Contribuições para a história lingüística do subgrupo Tupí-Guaraní Norte-Amazônica, com ênfase na língua Zo'é. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade de Brasília (orient. A. S. A. C. Cabral), 157 pp. https://repositorio.unb.br/handle/10482/13635
sources.note: Second-hand: pp. 26-27 summarizes Cabral 1996 (stress predictable, roots and particles stressed on last syllable); pp. 27-28 summarizes Cabral 2000: 'o escopo do acento é a palavra fonológica, que inclui a raiz e seus afixos flexionais, bem como os clíticos'; pp. 40-41 summarizes Cabral, Rodrigues & Carvalho 2010 (vowel devoicing restricted to pre-tonic syllables); p. 110: Zo'é 'conserva o acento final' (Rodrigues & Cabral 2002).

sources.citation: Jensen, Cheryl. 1999. Tupí-Guaraní. In Dixon & Aikhenvald (eds.), The Amazonian Languages, pp. 125-163. Cambridge: CUP.
sources.note: Family-level only: Proto-TG stress 'as in most of the descendent languages, occurred on the final syllable of the stem'; exceptions named (Chiriguano, subgroup 2, Wayampi, Asuriní do Tocantins). Zo'é mentioned only as a recently contacted language; no Zo'é-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Cabral, Ana Suelly Arruda Câmara. 1998. A propósito das oclusivas sonoras do Jo'é. Moara n. 9: 53-71 (jan./jun. 1998). https://periodicos.ufpa.br/index.php/moara/article/view/2944 (image-only PDF; scanned).
sources.note: Treats nasal vs oral 'acento' as suprasegmental phonemes; allophony of voiced stops stated relative to the 'sílaba tônica' of the theme; block quote pp. 55-56 says Guarayo, Chiriguano and Wayampí differ from the other TG languages 'nas quais o acento tônico recai sobre a sílaba final de temas'; all Jo'é examples carry final accent marks (bejú, asiarí, dadé, pidjé...). Does not restate a stress-placement rule for Jo'é as such.

sources.citation: SAPhon (South American Phonological Inventory Database), inventory page 'Zo'é' (pto), citing Cabral 2009 (Anais VI Congresso Abralin). https://linguistics.berkeley.edu/saphon/en/inv/
sources.note: Segment inventory only; 'Suprasegmental: None'; nothing on stress placement.

sources.citation: Cabral, Ana Suelly Arruda Câmara. 1996. Algumas evidências lingüísticas de parentesco genético do Jo'é com as línguas Tupí-Guaraní. Moara n. 4: 47-76. https://periodicos.ufpa.br/index.php/moara/article/view/3537 (scanned).
sources.note: Comparative (PTG reflexes in Jo'é); stress appears only as a conditioning environment in the sound-change table (*c > zero in unstressed position, *c > h under stress). No placement statement.
